messages:
nimbus.contact: Hey @support — we downloaded our weekend usage CSVs (2026-03-07 and 2026-03-08) from the SFTP export and both files only contain the header row. Dashboard shows tokens for those days and our invoice includes charges. Can you check?

emma_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the S3 path or manifest you got from the export? Also which account/org id is this?

nimbus.contact: SFTP deliverables link: s3://redwood-exports/nimbushealth/2026-03-07_2026-03-08/manifest.json
Manifest excerpt I grabbed:```
[
  {"path":"parts/2026-03-07/usage_00.csv","size":0},
  {"path":"parts/2026-03-07/usage_01.csv","size":0},
  {"path":"parts/2026-03-08/usage_00.csv","size":0},
  {"path":"parts/2026-03-08/usage_01.csv","size":0}
]```
All files return just the header: `customer_id,tokens,model,ts` then EOF. Dashboard shows ~12k tokens across the two days.

liam_cs: cc @olivia_billing so billing is aware. We need to confirm counts before telling customer about refunds/backfill.

emma_support: @raj_engdata can you take a look? Looks like the export manifest lists files but sizes are zero. We should check the export job run and the aggregation step for those dates.

raj_engdata: On it. Can you give me the export run id or the job window timestamps? I want the aggregator and the S3 writer logs. Also, any repro steps the customer did (downloaded from SFTP vs UI)?

nimbus.contact: We just pulled the SFTP zip via the support portal link. Downloaded both CSVs locally and opened in Excel. No manual edits.

eng-batch-bot: Export job 2026-03-08-03:01 triggered, run_id=exp-20260308-3, status=completed, manifest_written=true, upload_summary: 4 objects referenced, 4 objects uploaded, 0 bytes total (reported).

raj_engdata: Interesting — summary says 4 objects uploaded but 0 bytes total. That suggests the writer created zero-byte objects or the multipart commit did not finalize content. Can you paste near-real-time writer logs for run_id exp-20260308-3?

emma_support: Attached log snippet from the portal (redacted):```
[2026-03-08T03:00:57Z] export-run exp-20260308-3 started
[2026-03-08T03:01:12Z] aggregator: scan completed (rows=12034)
[2026-03-08T03:01:13Z] writer: creating temp object parts/2026-03-07/usage_00.csv.part
[2026-03-08T03:01:13Z] writer: write stream closed (bytes_written=0)
[2026-03-08T03:01:14Z] writer: rename temp -> parts/2026-03-07/usage_00.csv (size=0)
[2026-03-08T03:01:15Z] s3-client: multipart commit failed, retrying (error=ErrUnexpectedEOF)
[2026-03-08T03:01:16Z] writer: retry succeeded but stream empty (bytes_written=0)
[2026-03-08T03:01:18Z] export-run exp-20260308-3 completed, manifest written
```

raj_engdata: Thanks. This points to a transient I/O issue against the S3 endpoint during the writer window that led to commits being recorded with 0 bytes in the manifest. Notably aggregator scanned rows=12034 so the upstream counts exist. Two likely causes: 1) S3 client returned ErrUnexpectedEOF during multipart upload finalization and our writer incorrectly proceeded to record the final object path with zero bytes, or 2) the temp->final rename path is idempotent but lost payload after a retry path.

olivia_billing: From billing side, the invoice reflects recorded usage based on the aggregator totals (backend metering), not the exported CSV. So customer charges are correct and we should not issue refunds; instead we need to replace the CSVs and provide a corrected export. I'll hold on formal communications until eng confirms backfill plan.

raj_engdata: Proposed immediate actions:
- Recompute and backfill the two CSVs from raw events for 2026-03-07 to 2026-03-08 (run backfill job: `python backfill_export.py --start 2026-03-07 --end 2026-03-08 --target s3://redwood-exports/nimbushealth/2026-03-07_2026-03-08/`)
- Add a validation step post-upload to check object size > header_size and mark export-run as failed if sizes mismatch; do not write manifest entries for failed objects.
- Add retry safety: if multipart commit throws ErrUnexpectedEOF and subsequent retry yields zero bytes, abort and raise a rate-limited incident.

emma_support: That plan sounds good. Do you have an ETA for the recompute/backfill? Customer is asking for a replacement CSV now.

raj_engdata: I can kick the backfill now. Dry-run takes ~6m for this account, full run ~18m. I will: 1) run dry-run, 2) push final CSVs to a temporary path s3://redwood-exports/nimbushealth/repairs/2026-03-07_08/, 3) update manifest and let support push the file to the SFTP portal.

eng-batch-bot: Backfill job started: backfill-20260308-nimbus-1, status=running

ops-bot: Noting we saw elevated S3 ErrUnexpectedEOF retries cluster-wide 2026-03-08T03:00Z-03:05Z (network flaps to region us-west-2). Oncall notified earlier.

raj_engdata: Dry-run complete, row counts match aggregator (12034). Running final backfill now.

eng-batch-bot: Backfill job backfill-20260308-nimbus-1 completed successfully. New objects written to s3://redwood-exports/nimbushealth/repairs/2026-03-07_08/ (4 objects, total bytes=~1.2MB).

emma_support: @nimbus.contact I uploaded the repaired CSVs to your SFTP folder (path replaced with repaired files). Please re-download and confirm. Apologies for the inconvenience — we'll follow up with a postmortem and the change to prevent future zero-byte entries.

nimbus.contact: Got them — confirmed tokens line up with dashboard, opening the files looks good. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

olivia_billing: Confirming we will not change invoice. Sending a short note to the customer explaining discrepancy: export writer + transient S3 errors caused zero-byte CSVs, backend metering remained correct.

raj_engdata: Follow-ups for infra/eng: (1) add size validation before manifest write, (2) mark export-run failed if any object size <= header_size, (3) add metric export.writer.zero_bytes_count and an alert threshold, (4) investigate S3 client ErrUnexpectedEOF handling and make multipart commit idempotent. I created an RFC ticket: INFRA-5972.

liam_cs: Nice work team. I'll share the repaired files with Nimbus execs and close the loop. @emma_support please paste the canned explanation/snippet for customer email. :thumbsup:
